name: OpenAIRE
description: A community-based non-profit infrastructure providing open scholarly communication services across the research lifecycle, supporting a common European e-science environment.

coverage.notes: The OpenAIRE portfolio offers services for research lifecycle activities across countries, disciplines, and research actors — researchers, research performing organisations, policy-makers, publishers, funders, research communities, innovators, and infrastructures.

stakeholder-governed.notes: OpenAIRE is governed by an elected Executive Board and General Assembly, built on contributions and open discussions among member organisations.

non-discriminatory.notes: Membership is open to organisations or associations that commit to Open Science and align with the OpenAIRE mission; National Open Access Desks (NOADs) take part as Regular Members.

transparent-governance.notes: OpenAIRE is a Non-Profit Partnership (NPP) incorporated under Greek law; beyond this legal-status disclosure, governance-specific transparency detail is limited on the published assessment.

cannot-lobby.notes: OpenAIRE is a community-based non-profit with a mandate to push for Open Science, but does not lobby for its own infrastructure, following an inclusive approach that promotes any service or infrastructure supporting open science.

living-will.notes: OpenAIRE AMKE owns all software, data and services, which are all open; operation and maintenance can be split among member organisations and companies, and all necessary knowledge can be transferred at any time.

regular-review.notes: OpenAIRE has a statutory duration of twenty years within which it must complete its mission (art. 23) and wind down (art. 24) — a legally binding provision forcing periodic reassessment of its continued necessity.

transparent-operations.notes: “Partially implemented. OpenAIRE publishes its governance documents, policies and procedures openly, including its services sustainability models (subscriptions, free usage) and roadmaps.”

time-limited-funds.notes: OpenAIRE's main activities are still funded largely through third-party funding; it recognises the need to diversify income and has introduced hybrid financial models, including subscription plans for OpenAIRE CONNECT, MONITOR, and ARGOS.

generate-surplus.notes: OpenAIRE has an operational goal to develop a surplus of around 5–10% of its total revenue per year for the next five years.

financial-reserves.notes: OpenAIRE ensures that at any point in time it has reserves for three years of operation.

mission-consistent-revenue.notes: Revenue sources cover development of new features and services (funded by public or private open-science funders), administrative costs (by members), and service provision (by customers deploying open science services).

revenue-not-data.notes: OpenAIRE fully aligns with this principle by ensuring all underlying data used in its services remains openly accessible and treated as community-owned, with exceptions where privacy/GDPR is concerned.

volunteer-labour.notes: Not directly addressed in OpenAIRE's published v2 self-assessment.

transition-planning.notes: OpenAIRE acknowledges that reliance on individuals imposes risk, and has governance structures, committees and working groups in place to reduce single-point dependencies.

open-source.notes: The software powering OpenAIRE services results from the integration of open-source software solutions and is made available online via open software repositories.

open-secure-data.notes: All OpenAIRE-generated data is published as CC-BY or CC0, depending on the service and underlying data licensing dependencies.

available-preserved.notes: OpenAIRE-generated data is published via regular data dumps on Zenodo.org and via open REST APIs.

patent-non-assertion.notes: OpenAIRE's technical roadmap is committed to a patent non-assertion covenant policy.

interoperability-standards.notes: OpenAIRE uses open standards and supports interoperability (APIs, metadata standards, integrated OpenAIRE services), aligning with this principle.
